options: Animates the circle's creation over run_time.
Adds the circle instantly, with no motion.
Exports a single PNG frame to disk.
Pauses the scene for run_time seconds.
items.explanation: Create() is a creation animation: it draws the mobject onto the screen over run_time seconds. It is what puts the object on screen, unlike a raw property animation.

items.prompt: You call self.play(circle.animate.set_color(RED)) but circle was never created or added. What is the result?
options: No visible change, because the object is not on screen yet.
The circle appears and turns red automatically.
The scene pauses for one second.
items.explanation: A property animation like .animate only changes a mobject that is already on screen. You must Create/add it first; otherwise nothing is visible.

items.prompt: Write the command to render scene.py's HelloManim scene at low quality. (Type the full command.)
items.explanation: manim -ql scene.py HelloManim renders the named scene at low quality (-ql). Always pass the explicit scene name; avoid the interactive chooser in scripts.

items.prompt: Find the broken line and choose the fix.
items.code:
circle = Circle()
self.play(circle.animate.set_color(RED), run_time=0.5)
self.play(Create(circle), run_time=0.8)
self.wait(1.0)
options: Create the circle first, then animate its colour.
items.explanation: Line 2 animates a property of circle before line 3 ever puts circle on screen. The fix is to Create(circle) first, then animate its colour. Reordering fixes both the bug and the unreadable timing.

items.prompt: Which are required conventions from this lesson? (Select all that apply.)
options: Set run_time explicitly on important beats.
Animate every property, even at the cost of reading time.
items.explanation: The first three are enforced rules. The last is the opposite of the rule: pauses after reveals are mandatory precisely so the viewer has reading time.

items.prompt: Write a scene that shows a title and a square, with a deliberate pause after each reveal and a clean exit. Paste it below, then compare to the model answer and self-score.
items.modelAnswer:
from manim import *

class TitleAndSquare(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        self.camera.background_color = "#1C1C1C"
        title = Text("A title", font_size=48)
        square = Square(side_length=2.0, color=BLUE)
        self.play(Write(title), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1.0)
        self.play(Create(square), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(1.5)
        self.play(FadeOut(Group(*self.mobjects)), run_time=0.6)

rubric.criterion: Shows both a title and a square.
Every reveal is followed by a self.wait().
Mobjects are created before any property animation.
Uses a named background constant, not an inline magic hex.

items.explanation: The model obeys the lifecycle rule (create before animate), the pause-after-reveal rule, and the Group cleanup rule. Self-score honestly against the rubric.
